I am filing a complaint regarding Navy Federal Credit Unions denial of my fraud claim for an unauthorized debit card transaction in the amount of {$700.00} that occurred on XX/XX/year>. I reported this transaction as unauthorized, stating clearly that I had my debit card in my possession at all times, did not make or authorize the purchase, did not share my card information or PIN, and did not benefit from the transaction in any way. Navy Federal denied my claim, stating only that their information contradicts my claim of unauthorized activity. However, they have refused to provide any specific transaction-level evidence to support this conclusion. I have repeatedly requested documentation and details regarding their determination, including : - Method of authorization ( chip, swipe, or online ) - Whether a PIN was used - Transaction logs and timestamps - Merchant name and location details- Any device, IP address, or digital wallet information associated with the transaction In response, Navy Federal stated that they are unable to provide sensitive or internal information, including data from their internal systems. They have not provided any meaningful evidence showing that I authorized this transaction. Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( Regulation E ), financial institutions are required to conduct a reasonable investigation and determine whether a transaction was authorized. A generalized statement without supporting evidence does not meet this standard. I maintain that this transaction was unauthorized. The credit union has failed to provide sufficient justification for its denial and has not met its obligations under Regulation E. I am requesting that Navy Federal : 1. Provide the specific evidence used to determine that this transaction was authorized ; or 2. Reopen and properly reinvestigate my claim and issue a credit for the unauthorized transaction. I am seeking reimbursement of the {$700.00} and a proper resolution of this matter in accordance with federal law.

I immediately contacted Venmo support to understand the issue and resolve it. However, I was only given a generic response stating that they are unable to release the funds at this time and that the funds may be held for up to 180 days. I was not informed of any specific violation, suspicious transaction, or action on my part that caused this restriction. I was also not given any steps I could take to resolve the issue or expedite the release of my funds. As a result, I currently have no access to {$10000.00} of my own money, with no clear reason, timeline, or path to resolution provided by Venmo.

CONFLICTING AND MISLEADING EXPLANATIONS : When I asked for an explanation of the cost increases, I received conflicting answers from the broker team. I was first told the lock extension caused the credit removal, then told it was the investor switch. On XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXX XXXX, an attempted vehicle repossession occurred involving my vehicle, which is subject to a loan serviced by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX GM Financial ). The repossession was authorized by GM Financial and coordinated through XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, which in turn retained or dispatched a thirdparty repossession agent to carry out the repossession on its behalf. At the time of the incident, my vehicle was occupied by me and my minor child. The repossession agent lifted the vehicle while we were inside. I opened the vehicle door and informed the agent that the vehicle was occupied. I told the agent to back away because I was afraid and disclosed that I have mental health conditions. During this interaction, the agent made statements to the effect of youre scaring me because youre a XXXX. The agent then returned to the tow truck and stated that he was going to call the police. I repeatedly told the agent to put my vehicle down. The vehicle was not immediately lowered, but it was eventually lowered. After I made a verbal comment, the agent lifted the vehicle again and kept it hooked, despite having been informed that the vehicle was occupied and despite my repeated requests that the vehicle be put down. During this second lift, the vehicle shook while suspended, causing additional fear and instability while occupants were inside. Because the situation was escalating and unsafe, I called the police for assistance to stop the incident and deescalate the situation. I did not call the police to assist with repossession. When law enforcement arrived, the repossession agent remained on scene and continued to rely on police presence rather than disengaging from the repossession attempt. I also requested to remove my vehicle using my own tow service ( after breach of peace had occurred ) to resolve the situation peacefully, but that request was denied. I possess contemporaneous audio and video recordings capturing the incident, including evidence that the repossession agent was aware the vehicle was occupied prior to lifting it and evidence of the repeated lifting and breach of the peace. These materials are preserved. This was an attempted repossession. In total, my vehicle remained hooked to the tow truck for over an hour before the incident concluded and I was able to leave. As a direct result of this incident, I suffered physical, emotional, and psychological harm, including aggravation of a XXXX XXXX XXXX injury due to panicking and bracing myself during the incident, as well as aggravation of preexisting mental health conditions. My XXXX was also significantly affected by witnessing this event, and I am currently receiving therapy related to the incident. I submitted a formal complaint directly to GM Financial regarding this incident. GM Financial did not provide meaningful assistance, corrective action, or resolution. Instead, the issue was dismissed or deferred without addressing the unsafe and unlawful repossession conduct carried out by its authorized agents. This complaint concerns repossession misconduct by GM Financial and its agents, including attempting to repossess an occupied vehicle with a child present, failure to disengage after a clear breach of the peace, and threatening and intimidating conduct by the repossession agent. It also concerns GM Financial 's failure to properly vet, train, supervise, and control the repossession activity conducted on its behalf through XXXX XXXX XXXX and the assigned third party agent. The conduct violated federal fair debt collection standards, state law governing self help repossession, and the safety obligations a secured creditor owes when authorizing forcible recovery of collateral. I am requesting that the agency investigate GM Financial 's repossession assignment and oversight practices, the conduct of XXXX XXXX XXXX as a forwarding company, and the specific agent involved in this incident. This complaint is filed against XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

This email generated by Rocket Mortgage 's own system, sent from Rocket Mortgage 's own domain shows that the timestamp Rocket Mortgage cited as " XX/XX/XXXX '' in their CFPB response is simply XXXX XXXX Pacific time on XX/XX/XXXX misread by their Capital Markets system as XX/XX/XXXX EDT due to a time zone handling error. The lock expiration deadline was XX/XX/year> at XXXX XXXX PDT per Rocket Mortgage 's own CFPB response. The extension request was received at XXXX XXXX PDT on XX/XX/XXXX more than 13 hours before the deadline. Rocket Mortgage denied this rate lock extension based entirely on a time zone conversion error within their own internal Capital Markets system. The borrower was never late. The extension was timely by over 13 hours. 2. ROCKET MORTGAGE 'S OWN AUTOMATED SYSTEM CONFIRMED RECEIPT ON XX/XX/XXXX A separate earlier XXXX XXXX confirmation email was also transmitted to XXXX on XX/XX/year> at XXXX XXXX, confirming receipt of Case # XXXX, XXXX XXXX, Loan # XXXX. This email was generated automatically by Rocket Mortgage 's own platform the moment the request entered their system. Rocket Mortgage can not simultaneously have their system auto-generate a receipt confirmation on XX/XX/XXXX and claim they did not receive the request until XX/XX/XXXX. These two positions are irreconcilable, and are now definitively resolved by Exhibit E above. 3. ROCKET MORTGAGE 'S OWN PORTAL RECORDS SHOW SUBMITTED DATE OF XX/XX/year> Rocket Mortgage 's own XXXX XXXX portal shows the following for Case # XXXX : Submitted Date : XX/XX/year> Client Name : XXXX XXXX Loan Number : XXXX Type : XXXX XXXX This portal record is consistent with both confirmation emails and confirms XX/XX/XXXX as the submission date across all of Rocket Mortgage 's own systems except their Capital Markets system, which misread the timestamp due to a time zone error. 4. complaints.narrative: Subject : Formal Complaint regarding Regulation E Violation Unauthorized Reversal and Double Debit of Funds Incident Date : Thursday, XX/XX/year> Account Numbers involved : e-account ( ending in XXXX ) and Savings ( ending in XXXX ) Disputed Amount : {$320.00} ( Original transfer )/ {$320.00} ( Negative balance )/ {$320.00} ( Savings deduction ) Description of the Issue : On Thursday, XX/XX/year>, I received a transfer of {$320.00} from my daughter via XXXX XXXX into my e-account ( ending in XXXX ). The funds were explicitly shown as available, and I successfully transferred them the same day to my savings account ( ending in XXXX ). The banks systems would not have authorized these transactions if the funds were not fully cleared and available at that time. However, on the following day, the bank reversed the transaction without a valid explanation. This action resulted in a double loss of liquidity : 1. My e-account now reflects a negative balance of approximately - {$320.00}. 2. My savings account shows a simultaneous deduction of {$320.00}. Effectively, the bank has removed the funds from both accounts, leaving me with no access to the money and a total account discrepancy that exceeds the original transfer amount. Legal Basis for Complaint ( Regulation E ) : This situation constitutes a clear error in the handling of electronic fund transfers under 12 CFR 1005.11 ( Regulation E ). The bank failed to provide proper notice or a transparent justification for reversing a cleared electronic transfer. Furthermore, per 12 CFR 1005.11 ( c ), if the banks investigation into this error exceeds ten ( 10 ) business days, I am legally entitled to a provisional credit for the amount of the error while the investigation concludes. Financial Harm and Impact : The banks actions are causing immediate and ongoing financial damage. I have multiple scheduled obligations that rely on these funds, including : * XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Auto Loan ) : {$510.00} * XXXX XXXX ( Two payments ) : {$220.00} total XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX installment payments * XXXX XXXX XXXX Health plan ) and XXXX XXXX membership Due to this unjustified reversal, I am now facing the risk of returned payments, Non-Sufficient Funds ( NSF ) fees, late penalties, and damage to my credit score.

This reversal materially changed my account status and created an alleged delinquency that was not caused by my actions. Additionally, I had established automatic monthly payments ( autopay ) at the beginning of my loan in early XXXX. At no time did I authorize the cancellation or suspension of autopay. I have not signed, requested, or consented to stopping these automatic payments. I am requesting that Santander explain : - The exact date autopay was stopped - Whether the stop was system-generated or manually initiated - The reason autopay was discontinued - Why autopay was not reinstated after the reversal of the {$8100.00} payment - Whether any notice was provided to me regarding the suspension of autopay The unexplained suspension of autopay appears to have directly contributed to the alleged delinquency. If XXXX system actions caused payments to stop, then any resulting past-due status is inaccurate and should not be attributed to me. I sent a formal written dispute via certified mail, which was delivered and signed for on XX/XX/XXXX. Despite this, Santander has not provided a substantive response addressing these issues. Instead, I have continued to receive collection-related communications, including payment demands. Additionally, Santander processed my correspondence as a cease and desist request, which was not my intent. This has limited normal communication and may impede proper resolution of my dispute. I am requesting that Santander Consumer USA : 1. Conduct a full investigation into the {$8100.00} payment, including its source, authorization, and the basis for its reversal 2. Provide a complete account history and internal notes related to this transaction and autopay status 3. Provide documentation explaining the suspension of autopay and any related system or manual actions 4. Correct any inaccurate delinquency or negative reporting resulting from these issues 5. Restore my account to the correct status based on accurate information 6. Resume appropriate communication for the purpose of resolving this dispute

Supplemental Statement CFPB Complaint # XXXX Re : Valon Mortgage Inc. / XXXX XXXX XXXX I am submitting this supplemental statement to correct a factual error in my original complaint and to clarify and strengthen the arguments presented therein. In my original complaint, I stated that the XX/XX/XXXX appraisal was ordered through XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. I am correcting that statement. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX PMI department confirmed in writing on XX/XX/XXXX that the appraisal was ordered through XXXX, a third-party vendor, in connection with the partial release transaction not through XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX as required for XXXX termination purposes. I was not aware of this distinction at the time of my original submission. This correction does not weaken my complaint. It strengthens it. I. The Cost of the New Valuation Should Be Borne by the Servicer, Not the Borrower The need for a new XXXX-ordered valuation exists entirely because XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX servicing department ordered the XX/XX/XXXX appraisal through the wrong channel. XXXX XXXX XXXX ordered the appraisal through XXXX for the partial release transaction when had anyone in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX servicing operation coordinated with its own PMI department it would have been apparent that ordering through FanXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX system would have served both purposes simultaneously. XXXX XXXX XXXX 's own PMI department acknowledged this implicitly. Rather than simply denying my request and closing the matter, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX PMI representative XXXX XXXX emailed XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX to request an exception asking XXXX XXXX to accept the existing XXXX appraisal for PMI removal purposes. His XX/XX/XXXX email to me stated : " I have emailed XXXX requesting that they accept your appraisal for PMI removal. I am now awaiting XXXXXXXX XXXX reply as they hold the pen in this matter. '' This exception request was still active and unresolved when loan servicing transferred from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX to Valon Mortgage on XX/XX/XXXX. Standard servicing transfer protocols require the transferring servicer to convey all open requests and pending actions to the successor servicer. Valon inherited not just the loan but an open, mid-process exception request that XXXX XXXX XXXX had initiated on the borrower 's behalf. Whether Valon was made aware of this exception request through the transfer file or not, the borrower should not bear the cost of its abandonment. Valon has required me to pay {$190.00} for a new XXXX without ever indicating whether it reviewed the transfer file for open actions, whether the XXXX XXXX exception request was conveyed at transfer, or whether any attempt was made to continue pursuing it. Under 12 U.S.C. 4902 ( a ) ( 4 ), evidence requirements must be established in advance and communicated to the borrower promptly upon receipt of a cancellation request. The requirement for an XXXX-ordered valuation was not communicated to me at the time of my XX/XX/XXXX request and when it was finally communicated on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX own response was to pursue an exception rather than simply require me to pay for a new valuation. I request that the CFPB direct Valon Mortgage to : ( 1 ) determine the current status of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XX/XX/XXXX exception request to XXXX XXXX, and ( 2 ) if that exception was not resolved, pursue it to resolution before requiring the borrower to pay for a new valuation. complaints.product: Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service
complaints.narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Western Unions handling of a fraud report involving approximately {$4000.00} in money orders. After identifying clear signs of fraud in a rental transaction, I promptly reported the issue to Western Union on XX/XX/XXXX, before I was ever notified that the money orders had been negotiated. Despite my timely report and explicit request to stop the transaction, Western Union provided conflicting information, failed to provide meaningful updates, and ultimately allowed the money orders to be cashed on XX/XX/XXXX, approximately ten months after my fraud report. I was never notified of this negotiation and only became aware on XX/XX/XXXX, after repeatedly contacting Western Union and requesting documentation. After sending the money orders, I discovered discrepancies that raised immediate fraud concerns, including inconsistencies between the name on the drivers license, the name on the rental lease agreement, and the name associated with the bank information, all of which clearly indicated fraudulent activity. I contacted XXXX Bank and was informed that only Western Union could stop the money orders. On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Western Union, reported the suspected fraud, and requested that the money orders be stopped before negotiation. During this call, I received contradictory statements : I was first told the transaction could be stopped, then told it could not be stopped, and later told that the funds were frozen. I relied on the representation that the funds were frozen and inaccessible. Acting in good faith, I attempted to file a police report, which was declined due to jurisdictional complexity involving fraud, identity theft, cybercrime, and out-of-state activity. I also filed a complaint with the FBI IC3 system, sought legal advice, and repeatedly contacted Western Union for updates. Despite these efforts, I received no meaningful updates or resolution. After obtaining additional legal advice, I contacted Western Union again on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. After being transferred multiple times, I reached a XXXX XXXX representative who opened a formal report, provided copies of the endorsed money orders, and confirmed that the money orders had been cashed on XX/XX/XXXX. This was the first time I was made aware that the funds had been negotiated. This situation presents a serious and unresolved discrepancy. I reported fraud prior to negotiation and was told the funds were frozen, yet the funds were later cashed approximately ten months later. This raises critical questions about how the funds could be negotiated if they were truly frozen, or why I was told they were frozen if they were not. This reflects a clear procedural failure and inconsistent communication. At no point was I clearly notified that the money orders had been cashed, informed of the exact date of negotiation, properly advised of my right to file an Affidavit of Forgery, or informed of any applicable deadlines. I was initially presented with a prequalification offer of 4.80 % APR for 72 months at {$400.00} per month on a loan amount of {$25000.00} on XX/XX/year>. Based on this offer, I authorized Autopay to perform a hard credit inquiry on my account. Following the hard credit pull, Autopay significantly changed the terms of the offer without explanation on XX/XX/year>. The new offer presented was 7.49 % APR for 75 months at {$450.00} per month an increase of 2.69 percentage points from the prequalified rate. The refinance would have provided no financial benefit whatsoever. When I questioned the change in rate, the Autopay representative used high-pressure sales tactics, stating that 7.49 % was the lowest rate I would qualify for and pressuring me to accept the offer immediately or else any future inquiries about a refinance loan from any other companies would be declined immediately. When I requested that loan documents be sent to me for review prior to making a decision, Autopay refused to provide any written documentation. From my basic understanding, refusal to provide loan documents for review prior to signing may constitute a violation of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), which requires clear written disclosure of loan terms before a consumer enters into a credit agreement. I am requesting that the CFPB investigate Autopay 's prequalification and rate change practices, as this pattern of presenting favorable rates to obtain hard credit inquiries and then delivering significantly worse terms appears designed to pressure consumers into accepting unfavorable loan agreements. I have not signed any agreement with Autopay and have rejected their offer.

I am submitting this complaint regarding unauthorized credit card accounts opened in my name without my knowledge or consent and the lenders failure to meet its obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). While I was married, my XXXX XXXX opened one or more credit card accounts in my name without my authorization. I did not apply for these accounts, did not use them, and was unaware they existed until after she stopped making payments and I began receiving late and delinquency notices. I reported this matter to Chase as fraud and identity theft and formally disputed the accounts. Chase rejected my claim, stating that because prior payments were made from a joint bank account, the accounts are not considered fraudulent. This rationale is incorrect and inconsistent with FCRA standards. Payment from a joint account does not establish that I authorized the opening of credit in my name or had knowledge the accounts existed. Under the FCRA, furnishers are required to conduct a reasonable investigation when a consumer disputes the accuracy or authorization of an account. I specifically requested that Chase review objective application and transaction data, including IP addresses and other identifying information associated with the credit applications and account activity, to determine whether I was involved. Chase has not provided evidence that I applied for or authorized these accounts, nor have they demonstrated that a reasonable investigation was performed. Despite my dispute, negative information related to these unauthorized accounts is being reported and/or threatened to be reported to the credit bureaus. As a result, I am being held responsible for debt I did not knowingly incur, causing ongoing credit and financial harm. I am requesting CFPB intervention to ensure compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including : A proper and documented reinvestigation of the disputed accounts Removal of unauthorized accounts from my responsibility Correction and suppression of any inaccurate or adverse credit reporting Confirmation that lack of authorization to open credit can not be overridden solely by payment source The lenders current position improperly conflates access to shared funds with consent to open credit, which does not meet FCRA requirements for accuracy or reasonable investigation.

complaints.issue: Advertising and marketing, including promotional offers
complaints.narrative: On XX/XX/year>, I attended a dental appointment at XXXX XXXX in XXXX, North Dakota. At the conclusion of the appointment, office staff presented me with a treatment plan and enrolled me in a CareCredit financing agreement on the practice premises without providing any written disclosure of the credit terms at the time of signing. Specifically : No written disclosures were provided at or before signing. I was not given any documentation at the time of the transaction describing the interest rate, annual percentage rate ( XXXX ), repayment schedule, minimum payment obligations, deferred interest terms, or any other material credit terms required under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), Regulation XXXX. I was told disclosures would arrive weeks later ; I was not sent any emails or sent home with any packets as I expected. When I asked about documentation, I was told verbally by office staff that I would receive the CareCredit card in XXXX to XXXX business days and that a letter from CareCredit would arrive approximately XXXX to 25 days after that. This does not constitute timely written disclosure as required by federal law. Regulation XXXX requires that the creditor deliver or mail required disclosures at the time of or before consummation of the transaction not weeks afterward. The signing process was conducted under deceptive conditions. During the signing of the financing agreement, the staff member physically covered the portion of the tablet screen displaying the document with her hand, preventing me from reading the terms before signing. I specifically asked, " I'll be getting a copy of all of this I'm signing, then? '' and was told yes. No copy of the credit agreement was provided at that time. I was not advised of my right to cancel. I was not informed at any point during the signing process that I had the right to cancel the agreement, nor was I given any documentation outlining a cancellation window. I have since initiated cancellation of the CareCredit account within the five-business-day period, but only because I independently researched my rights after leaving the office. I was a XXXX first-time dental patient attending an appointment alone. I was presented with a financing agreement following a stressful and confusing appointment, in a private office, with no written terms, no explanation of my rights, and no opportunity to review what I was signing. The manner in which this agreement was obtained including the physical obstruction of the document and the absence of any written disclosures raises serious concerns about whether informed, voluntary consent to the credit terms was possible under these circumstances.

The complainant is the recipient of an XX/XX/XXXX letter from Ally Bank identifying him personally as a guarantor on Ally account ending in the last XXXX digits of the agreement number. '' XXXX of XXXX were voided the same day XXXX signed. XXXX written requests for explanation went unanswered. Ally then granted a supervisor escalation on XX/XX/XXXX that never occurred. While the complainant was waiting for that escalation, Ally repossessed the vehicle on XX/XX/XXXX from the complainant 's wife ( not a party to the loan ) at her workplace, a public elementary school in XXXX XXXX, with no advance notice through any channel including the active email channel through which Ally and the complainant had been corresponding. XXXX redeemed the obligation by wire of {$6800.00} on XX/XX/XXXX. Ally confirmed receipt the same day on a recorded call and confirmed that the security interest was released and the release form uploaded to the recovery agent ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ). XXXX XXXX XXXX Ally 's collateral management vendor, separately confirmed receipt of the release paperwork. As of this filing, more than XXXX hours after Ally 's confirmed release, the vehicle remains in XXXXXXXX XXXX physical possession. XXXX has not responded to XXXX written communications from the complainant requesting confirmation of the release paperwork and an appointment to retrieve the vehicle. XXXX bypassed the complainant 's correspondence channel to call his wife rather than respond in writing. Ally XXXX XXXX XXXX acknowledged the matter on XX/XX/XXXX ( file XXXX ) but has not addressed the ongoing retention. The Ally XXXX currently displays the account as " XXXX XXXX '' with a total balance of {$61000.00} and a next payment of {$1600.00} due XX/XX/XXXX. The redemption cured the default and reinstated the loan. The account should not display as past due as of any date before XX/XX/XXXX. The displayed payment amount is also the original payment of {$1600.00} rather than the modified payment of {$1400.00} that XXXX had bargained for in the XXXX voided modification agreements. If the past-due designation is currently being reported to consumer reporting agencies, that raises FCRA furnisher concerns under 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2. The XX/XX/XXXX cover letter, received XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX days before the scheduled XX/XX/XXXX auction, identifies the complainant personally as " a guarantor on this account. '' The communication identifies itself as from a debt collector. No guaranty document exists in the complainant 's records. The vehicle is registered and insured to XXXX alone, the loan does not appear on the complainant 's personal credit report, and the modification correspondence and signature blocks throughout the workout cycle were directed exclusively to XXXX through the complainant in his representative capacity. The assertion of personal guarantor liability against an individual without supporting documentation, in a formal collection communication, implicates 15 U.S.C. 1692e and XXXX. The pattern of issuing modification agreements through the workout team while the collection function moved toward repossession, with no coordination between the XXXX, presents the factual structure the XXXX has identified as dual tracking. The framework is well developed in mortgage servicing and the analysis applies to auto finance servicing where the lender holds itself out as offering workout opportunities. complaints.issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
complaints.narrative: I am submitting this formal complaint to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) to report a fraudulent debt collection attempt involving identity theft. A lawsuit has been filed against me by TENAGLIA & HUNT, P.A., representing XXXX XXXX XXXX, the assignee of a debt allegedly owed to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, in the amount of {$3300.00} and/or any other amount. I am not the debtor in this case. I have never entered into any contract or financial obligation with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, nor have I incurred any debt to them. This lawsuit is based on fraudulent activity where my personal information was unlawfully used by an identity thief without my consent. I did not authorize any of the transactions or account openings associated with this alleged debt. The legal action being pursued against me is an unjust attempt to collect a debt that does not belong to me, and I have never received any goods, services, or benefits from the transactions made under this fraudulent account. As a victim of identity theft, I should not be held liable for debts that are not mine. This situation has caused me significant emotional distress as I am being unjustly accused and harassed for a debt created through the wrongful use of my personal information. The actions of XXXX XXXX XXXX, and TENAGLIA & HUNT, P.A. violate several consumer protection laws. The fraudulent claim is a violation of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692, which requires debt collectors to validate the debt before pursuing legal action. XXXX XXXX, XXXX, and their representatives have failed to validate the debt and continue to pursue a lawsuit based on fraudulent information. Additionally, the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681, provides protections regarding the accuracy of credit information. XXXX XXXX and TENAGLIA & HUNT have failed to ensure the legitimacy of the debt and have not properly investigated its origin, which violates my rights under the FCRA. Furthermore, under the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act ( FACTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2, victims of identity theft can challenge fraudulent accounts and require creditors to remove them. XXXX XXXX and TENAGLIA & HUNT have continued pursuing this fraudulent debt, disregarding FACTA protections. Moreover, this situation involves fraudulent misrepresentation. TENAGLIA & HUNT and XXXX XXXX are knowingly attempting to collect a debt that I do not owe. They have failed to investigate the legitimacy of the debt, and their pursuit constitutes fraud. Their actions have resulted in unjust enrichment, unlawfully attempting to benefit from a debt that is not mine. The emotional toll this situation has caused has been severe. The constant worry about my financial future and the distress of being wrongfully pursued have negatively impacted my mental and emotional well-being. This situation has caused significant XXXX, frustration, and helplessness. I now struggle with sleepless nights while trying to clear my name. I am submitting this complaint to the CFPB to report these fraudulent actions and to request immediate intervention. I ask that the CFPB take appropriate action to ensure that XXXX XXXX and TENAGLIA & HUNT cease their illegal collection efforts, protect my rights as a victim of identity theft, and hold those responsible accountable under the law. I respectfully request the immediate dismissal of this case.

I am filing this complaint regarding the handling and denial of my Capital One XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The claim was administered by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and relates to a credit card benefit underwritten by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. My claim was filed on XX/XX/XXXX. I cooperated with the claim process and provided documentation and explanations in good faith, including wireless billing documentation, proof of card payment, proof of replacement, proof of travel, proof regarding my primary carrier coverage limitations, and written explanations regarding the circumstances of the loss. The problem is that the administrators documentation requests changed over time. Initial requests concerned wireless billing statements and proof of card payment. Later requests concerned carrier insurance, carrier claim denial/deductible proof, and travel documentation showing I was abroad at the time of the incident. Only later did the administrator request a diagnostic report. The diagnostic report was not reasonably obtainable under the circumstances. At the time of the incident, I was traveling in XXXX. I attempted to explore service options, but was advised that diagnosing/opening the U.S. model internationally could potentially cause further damage and would take approximately two days. Because I needed a functioning phone immediately while traveling, proceeding with that diagnostic was not feasible, and I purchased a replacement device out of pocket. I did not ignore the diagnostic request or fail to cooperate. I explained that the requested diagnostic was not reasonably obtainable. Despite this, the administrator denied the claim on XX/XX/XXXX, stating that additional documentation requested was not received within the timeframe listed in the Guide to Benefits. I believe this denial mischaracterizes the claim record. This was not a failure to submit available documentation. It was a situation where the later-requested diagnostic report was not reasonably obtainable, and I explained that before denial. The administrator also continued requesting the diagnostic in XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX without clearly stating that the claim had expired or that further documentation/explanations would no longer be accepted. This continued processing reasonably indicated that the claim remained active and under review. I requested a policy-based explanation for the denial, including the exact Guide to Benefits provision relied on, the exact deadline date applied, the exact date of loss used to calculate the deadline, and an explanation of why the claim was denied for untimely documentation even though I had explained that the requested diagnostic report was not reasonably obtainable under the circumstances. I also asked them to explain why they continued requesting documentation in XXXX and XXXX if they considered the claim already ineligible due to the documentation deadline. I am requesting that Capital One review the handling of this benefit claim, require a policy-based review by the benefit administrator, reopen or reconsider the claim, and evaluate it based on the documentation and explanations already submitted.

Complaint Against Debt Collector Regarding Refusal to Honor Written Settlement Offer I am filing this complaint regarding a debt collectors refusal to honor the written terms of a settlement offer that was provided directly to me. I received a written settlement communication from the company that contained language offering a settlement based on 20 % of the balance. The wording was clear and unambiguous as written. After reviewing the offer, I relied upon the exact language contained in the document in evaluating and responding to the proposed settlement terms. After I attempted to proceed based on the written language of the offer, the company informed me that the phrase 20 % of was supposedly intended to read 20 % off and claimed the language was merely a typographical error. The company is now refusing to honor the terms exactly as they were presented in the written settlement correspondence. My concern is not merely that an error may have occurred, but that the company expects consumers to disregard or reinterpret official written settlement communications after the fact. Consumers should be able to reasonably rely on the plain language contained in formal collection and settlement notices without later being told the terms were different than what was actually written. As the drafting party, the debt collector bears responsibility for ensuring that its settlement communications are accurate before being transmitted to consumers. In my view, refusing to honor the written language after it has been issued creates a misleading and unfair situation for consumers attempting to resolve debts in good faith. I requested that the company provide : A copy of the original settlement offer ; A detailed explanation of the alleged typographical error ; The date the error was discovered ; Documentation showing whether corrected notices were issued to other consumers ; and Confirmation that no adverse credit reporting or collection activity would occur while this dispute remains unresolved. To date, the company has refused to honor the settlement language as written. I am requesting that the CFPB review this matter for potentially misleading or unfair debt collection and settlement practices and assist in ensuring that the company honors the written settlement terms provided. Attached documentation includes copies of the settlement correspondence and related communications regarding the dispute.

My FHA-insured mortgage on my primary residence was originally serviced by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX . On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX approved me for an FHA Special Forbearance Plan covering 12 monthly installments from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX. Under the plan, my contractual monthly Total Payment Due was {$0.00}. XXXX confirmed in writing that no late charges would be assessed and that I would be reported to credit bureaus as current and in a forbearance plan. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX issued a written notice confirming that my FHA Special Forbearance Plan was complete. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX issued a formal written notice stating : " We have sufficient information to evaluate you for a loan modification, and we consider your application complete as of XX/XX/XXXX. '' The notice expressly acknowledged that XXXX was prohibited from initiating any foreclosure-related notice or filing while the complete application was under review, and committed to a decision no later than XX/XX/XXXX. Before XXXX completed the loss mitigation evaluation, my loan was transferred to Carrington Mortgage Services , LLC . The pending modification review had not been completed by XXXX before transfer. Under 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( k ), Carrington was required as the transferee servicer to honor the complete loss mitigation application that XXXX received on XX/XX/XXXX, and to continue the evaluation rather than restart or cancel it. Carrington has since taken the following actions, each of which I believe violates federal mortgage servicing law and FHA loss mitigation requirements : ( 1 ) Carrington demanded lump-sum repayment of the entire forborne amount and threatened foreclosure. FHA loss mitigation guidance under HUD Handbook 4000.1 does not permit servicers to require lump-sum repayment of forborne amounts as a precondition for bringing an FHA-insured loan current. Multiple FHA loss mitigation options including the COVID-19 Recovery Modification, FHA-HAMP, Standalone Partial Claim, and Recovery Standalone Partial Claim must be evaluated before foreclosure can proceed. ( 2 ) Carrington cancelled my complete loss mitigation application without providing any written notice or written decision. During a phone call, Carrington informed me that my application had been cancelled because they had attempted to call me for a " second attestation '' and I did not answer. I never received any written request from Carrington for additional documentation, any written request for an attestation, or any written notice of cancellation. This violates 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( c ), which requires a written decision stating the specific reason for any denial of a complete loss mitigation application. It also violates 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( b ) ( 2 ) ( i ) ( B ), which requires the servicer to provide written notice specifying what additional information is needed and a reasonable deadline to provide it. A missed phone call is not a permitted basis for cancellation under Regulation X. ( 3 ) On XX/XX/XXXX, Carrington issued a Maryland Notice of Intent to Foreclose under Maryland Real Property Article 7-105.1 ( c ). The notice lists my Date of Default as XX/XX/XXXX a date that falls within my active XXXX FHA Special Forbearance Plan, during which my contractual monthly payment was {$0.00}. The notice claims my loan is 269 days past due and demands {$21000.00} to cure. Carrington appears to have re-characterized forbearance-period suspended installments as delinquent payments after taking over servicing, contrary to the written terms of the XXXX forbearance plan and contrary to XXXXXXXX XXXX written confirmation that I would be reported as current and in a forbearance plan. Carrington also elected not to offer prefile mediation. Under the Notice of Intent to Foreclose, a foreclosure action ( Order to Docket ) may be filed in Circuit Court as early as XX/XX/XXXX. ( 4 ) Carrington has not provided me with a single point of contact for my loss mitigation file, in violation of 12 C.F.R. 1024.40. ( 5 )

Ally Financial is attempting to collect an alleged auto loan deficiency balance without providing legally required validation under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and without providing any documentation showing that I am legally responsible for this debt. They also failed to provide required repossession and sale documents under UCC Article 9. What happened? On XX/XX/year>, I sent Ally Financial a written request for validation of an alleged deficiency balance related to auto loan account. My request specifically asked for : A complete copy of the original signed retail installment contract bearing my signature The VIN, year, make, and model of the vehicle A full payment history The repossession notice, notice of sale, and all disposition documents A detailed deficiency balance calculation, including sale proceeds and fees Proof that Ally Financial has the legal right to collect this alleged debt On XX/XX/year>, Ally responded but did not provide : The signed contract Any document bearing my signature The repossession notice The notice of sale Sale/disposition documentation A deficiency calculation Proof of legal right to collect They only provided payment history, basic vehicle information, and confirmation of repossession and chargeoff. They also stated they reported the account to credit bureaus and recently marked it as disputed. Why this is a problem : Ally has not validated the debt as required by 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ). Without the signed contract or any documentation establishing liability, they can not legally continue collection activity or report the debt as valid. Additionally, the divorce decree awarded the vehicle to my exspouse, who had exclusive possession and responsibility for the vehicle. I had no access to the vehicle, no ability to prevent repossession, and no benefit from it after the divorce. Ally has provided no documentation showing that I agreed to this loan or that I had any responsibility for the vehicle after the divorce. Despite failing to validate the debt, Ally continues to report the account to credit bureaus and has not closed the account. What I am requesting from the CFPB : I am requesting that the CFPB require Ally Financial to : Provide full validation of the alleged debt or acknowledge that they can not validate it Cease all collection activity Remove all negative credit reporting related to this account Close the account in full due to inability to validate liability for either party Confirm in writing that no further collection or reporting will occur Ally has not met their legal obligations under the FDCPA or UCC Article 9, and they are reporting an unvalidated debt to credit bureaus. I am requesting CFPB assistance to resolve this matter.

I am the victim of identity theft. I have made multiple attempts at disputing the accounts and the charges with the banks in question and each time they " investigate '' they come back with a determination that the accounts are valid but refuse to provide evidence to back this up. In this particular case, I am referring to Navy Federal Credit Union. I had one credit card with them that was little used at the time. There was no balance to my knowledge at the time the ID theft occurred. The credit card was apparently hacked and used. All of this seems to have occurred after a massive hospital data breach and a hacking into my cell phone. I have filed disputes and identity theft with them multiple times. Each time they say that their internal investigation has determined the debt to be valid. I have requested, in writing, the evidence used to base their determination on. They refuse or ignore my requests and have since submitted my account to collections and charged it off. I am being held accountable for a debt that I have disputed multiple times in writing while requesting evidence, only to be told that they have verified the account is mine but can provide absolutely no evidence to back this up. I have filed and provided police reports and IDTHEFT.GOV reports on the identity theft as well. I had likewise indicated to them, and as was noted in the police report filed in XXXX XXXX and on IDTHEFT, gov, my phone had already been cloned/hacked and used on multiple accounts. Said phone was often, during the time of this account being opened and used, resetting itself, refreshing, and acting in a manner beyond my control. I had to change not just phone numbers but complete phone due to the theft that had occurred in my name. All of this was revealed to this credit card company. The card was not opened by me, nor was I aware of it. The theft was very sophisticated as they even, on some opened cards, mimicked similar purchases to what they had gleaned from other cards I actually owned. These accounts were not opened by me and are not mine. These cases do happen, they may not be the most common form of fraud but these sophisticated id theft tactics do occur, have been documented and should be well-known to credit card company fraud departments. I demand that this credit information be permanently removed from my credit report and from my name.

complaints.narrative: NOTICE OF DISPUTED TRANSACTION AND DEMAND FOR INVESTIGATION Date : XXXX Product : Credit Card / Promotional Financing Company : Comenity Capital Bank Complaint : I am filing this complaint regarding a disputed timeshare transaction financed through Comenity Capital Bank in connection with a sales presentation conducted by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. My wife and I are senior citizens. I am nearly XXXX XXXX XXXX and suffer from XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. My wife is also in her XXXX and battling XXXX. We were subjected to an extended, high-pressure sales presentation lasting several hours despite repeatedly declining the offer multiple times. We were eventually persuaded into signing financing documents for approximately {$17000.00} through Comenity Capital Bank during the same sales process. The financing arrangement included a deferred-interest promotional structure under which no interest would be charged until XX/XX/year>, but if the balance is not fully paid by that date, approximately 24 % retroactive interest is imposed from the original date of purchase. We do not believe this financing structure was adequately or fairly explained considering the pressure tactics used during the sales process. We believe the underlying transaction was induced through material misrepresentations, including statements concerning : The nature and value of the timeshare program Ease of cancellation or exit Financial benefits and affordability Whether the obligation could affect family members after death Long-term financial impact Availability of future relief options The financing was arranged directly during the sales presentation and appeared to be integrated into the sales process. We believe the lender benefited directly from the disputed transaction. We are now facing the threat of substantial retroactive interest charges unless the entire balance is paid immediately, despite the underlying transaction being actively disputed with the seller and reported to consumer protection agencies. We are requesting the following : Immediate investigation into the financing and sales practices associated with this transaction. Suspension of retroactive deferred-interest charges while the transaction remains disputed. Suspension of collection activity and negative credit reporting during investigation. Review of whether the deferred-interest disclosures were adequately presented under these circumstances. Copies of all signed financing agreements, disclosures, electronic signatures, and related documentation. Review of the relationship between the lender and the merchant involved in this transaction. Consideration of hardship protections due to age, medical conditions, and consumer vulnerability. We believe this transaction involved deceptive and unfair practices targeting elderly consumers and request CFPB assistance before substantial retroactive interest charges are imposed. This notice constitutes a formal written dispute of the underlying transaction and related financing obligations. Sincerely

On approximately XXXX XXXX XXXX I discovered the direct deposit of my Social Security check to my band checking account was not happening. As a result, the first six deposits intended for our account from SSA were accepted by Chase and went to another account at Chase Bank. 
 Upon discovery XXXX XXXX XXXX, we immediately made phone calls to both the SSA and Chase Bank. These telephone calls did not render a solution so we made an in person visit to a Chase branch in XXXX XXXX California. At that first visit to Chase they seemed willing too look into the matter.  XXXX XXXX we had to travel to Colorado so on XXXX XXXX we went to a Chase branch in XXXX, Colorado to continue looking in to the problem. In XX/XX/year>, I made substantial principal/payoff-related payments toward my mortgage loan in an effort to fully satisfy the loan early, including large principal payments in addition to regularly scheduled payments. By early XX/XX/year>, the remaining balance had been reduced to {$28.00} and I paid the {$28.00}, however, automatic payments continued to draft and interest continued accruing while the payoff was still being processed. During this time, I contacted the company multiple times because I believed the loan had effectively been paid off. I continued receiving collection-style calls and received inconsistent verbal information from representatives regarding whether the loan was fully resolved, whether additional amounts were due, and whether I would be receiving a refund or overpayment check. The continued automatic drafting after my payoff attempts, combined with the transaction reversals, suspense balances, late fee assessment, and loan paid in full entries, created significant confusion regarding the true status of the loan and payoff process. A primary concern is the length of time it took for the loan payoff to be fully processed and closed despite the substantial payments already made in XX/XX/year>. During this extended payoff period, interest continued accruing and automatic drafts continued, which contributed to the confusion regarding the final payoff amount and status of the account. I also do not believe a late fee should have been assessed under these circumstances, particularly while automatic payments remained active and substantial payoff payments had already been made. Although the late fee was later waived, its assessment further contributed to the confusion surrounding the payoff process. Because of the continued drafting, reversal activity, and contradictory verbal information provided by representatives, I remain concerned that the loan payoff may not have been accurately or timely reconciled and that potential overpayments may not have been fully addressed or explained. Although the company later provided transaction histories and payoff statements, I believe the payoff handling and communication process was unclear and poorly explained while it was occurring. I acknowledge that the late fee was ultimately waived and the remaining shortage was expensed by the company. However, I am submitting this complaint due to the confusing payoff process, extended delay in closing the loan, continued automatic drafting after payoff attempts, possible unreconciled overpayment concerns, and contradictory information provided during the servicing of the loan payoff.

complaints.product: Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service
complaints.narrative: On XX/XX/XXXX I received a text from a number identifying themselves as XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX and was alerted to fraudulent activity on my account. The text asked if {$1100.00} charged to XXXX was me. I typed no then the next text said no further action was needed and a representative would reach out to review. I googled if XXXX texts their customers and they do. The representative then called me and went over numerous charges in other states to which I declined making. He then said because my XXXX account was tied to my Chase account ( which it is so it sounded very believable ) he would put me in contact with someone from JP Morgan. Then someone claiming to be from JP Morgan Chase XXXX department named XXXX went over numerous pending transactions ( XXXX $ worth ), none of which I had made. In order to protect my funds he instructed me to transfer my remaining money to XXXX alias accounts because he told me they were conducting an internal investigation due to suspecting a bank employee at my local branch was helping to commit fraud. He told me the alias names were under my account and I would have access to them within XXXX hours. These accounts did not have separate routing numbers therefore it wasnt immediately setting off alarm bells. This individual was able to tell me my local bank address, my social security, my birthday, and address so it felt incredibly legitimate. I then out of nervousness went to the Chase bank in XXXX to ask for a wire transfer instead of a member to member transfer. The exact first amount was {$45000.00} to be wired to the alias account in XXXX XXXX name with account number XXXX. I have never wired money or initiated a member to member transfer so I wasnt aware of the protocol or differences. During the first wire transfer the bank teller XXXX did not ask for a routing number, an address, etc. She did ask how the funds would be used to which I said personal use. She did not ask me how I intended to get the funds or made me aware that I was not an authorized user on the alias account. Once I looked back over the paperwork I also noticed she failed to have me read, sign, or date the how to spot fraud paperwork that is included in the wire transfer agreement. She also failed to fill out the XXXX approval section of the document. The scammer had me on the phone this entire time mind you. The scammer then instructed me to cancel the wire and go back to ask for a member to member transfer. I went ahead and did that again without any questions from the tellers. Then XXXX instructed me to make another member to member transfer at the XXXX XXXX. I went ahead and drove to XXXX to again do the same process. Here I asked for a {$42000.00} transfer to alias account XXXX XXXX. Again no questions were asked of me so I figured everything was legitimate. XXXX insisted that the member to member transfer was faster and more efficient. On XX/XX/XXXX XXXX from Chase arranged a call back with me and made me aware that the scammer was still trying to access my funds therefore I should move the remaining money. At this moment it clicked for me that something was not right. I then immediately drove back to the XXXX chase to make them aware of the fraud. There the teller ( her name is on the member to member receipt I brought the police ) said oh I had bad feeling and should have said something but didnt - my significant other was present for this conversation and can attest to this. There the fraud department told me my claim was denied and I was offered XXXX support from the bank staff. Then I went directly to the police station to fill out a report. After that we went back to the XXXX branch to make them aware of the situation. They instructed me to call the fraud department who then hung up on us both personally and then again hung up on the bank tellers. At this point XXXX of the tellers was able to escalate my issue and specifically told me ALL funds had been successfully frozen and neither I or the scammer could reach

complaints.narrative: On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent XXXX USDT ( approximately {$34000.00} ) to a Coinbase deposit address using the XXXX network. Coinbase 's own help documentation at the time indicated XXXX was a supported network. Two Coinbase Support agents ( XXXX and XXXX ) responded the same day. XXXX explicitly assured me in writing that the {$34000.00} USDT would arrive in my account, stating XXXX XXXX in direct response to my question about whether the funds would arrive, and We don't make fake promises. Subsequent emails from Coinbase Support on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX contained explicit written commitments : While there is nothing Coinbase can do to recover these funds for you at this time, if we do add this network to our platform these funds will be automatically credited to your account. If this network is supported in the future but you still do not see your funds, please reach back out to us about crediting these funds to your account. Coinbase has since added XXXX support to its platform. The funds were not automatically credited. I followed Coinbase 's explicit reach-out instruction in XXXX, which is the basis for cases # XXXX and # XXXX, and the subsequent formal complaint. Coinbase 's denial reasoning has shifted across four written communications, with the most recent finally confirming the actual basis : On XX/XX/XXXX, Coinbase Support denied recovery citing the XXXX XXXX XXXX as a technical impediment, claiming the funds were permanently unrecoverable. After I explained that the XXXX upgrade was a seamless state migration ( not a chain split ) and the funds remained at the same address on current XXXX, Coinbase issued a revised response the same day acknowledging your explanation around the XXXX XXXX upgrade is thoughtful and makes sense from a pure on-chain perspective and admitting the balance still appears on-chain. That email reframed the denial as : we do not have an approved recovery process. After I filed a formal complaint, Coinbase issued a final decision on XX/XX/XXXX that again attempted to characterize the denial as technical, stating : This is not a policy-based decision it is a technical limitation. The XXXX and pXXXX XXXXXXXX networks handle transactions differently at a protocol level. I replied requesting reconciliation between the conflicting denials. On XX/XX/XXXX, Coinbase Customer Support issued a written response that directly contradicts the XX/XX/XXXX technical framing and confirms the denial is a policy decision. Key direct quotes : The authoritative position is that this is a limitation of Coinbase 's supported processes and infrastructure, not a literal protocol-level impossibility on XXXX. Your XX/XX/XXXX email stating that we do not have an approved recovery process for this class of XXXX XXXX deposits is the more accurate framing. The XX/XX/XXXX wording about a 'technical limitation at a protocol level ' was imprecise and I apologize for that. You are absolutely right that the XXXX upgrade was a seamless state migration ( not a chain split ). Your USDT remains at the same deposit address on XXXX XXXX ( chain ID XXXX ). The balance is visible today on XXXX as current on-chain state, not as some archived XXXX ' network. When Coinbase added XXXX and later XXXX on XXXX, we chose not to backfill or onboard XXXX XXXX deposits into our internal ledgers and recovery tooling. The address you cited is recognized within Coinbase as a custodial deposit address used in our infrastructure. The fact that you successfully received a later Ethereum USDT deposit to the same address is consistent with that. Even if, in theory, a manual sweep transaction could be crafted, Coinbase can only perform recoveries that run through approved, audited tooling. Coinbase does not support ad-hoc, one-off manual sweeps outside of those established flows, even when funds are visible on-chain. I have independently verified via XXXX that {$33000.00} in token holdings remain at the Coinbase-controlled deposit address ( XXXX ) as of XX/XX/X

Because this cancellation was necessitated entirely by the lender 's non-compliant practices, I expect zero cancellation fees, appraisal fees, or other charges to be assessed to my account, and I request a formal regulatory review of their TRID and FCRA compliance practices.

I am filing this complaint to bring attention to what I believe was an unfair or misleading mortgage-servicing practice that could harm other borrowers. I wired {$140000.00} to Planet Home Lending , LLC for my mortgage loan, loan number XXXX. The wire instructions specifically stated Apply to Principal. This was intended as a principal-only curtailment, not a payoff. After the funds were sent, I was contacted and told Planet Home Lending was treating the payment as a payoff. I clarified that this was incorrect and that the payment was intended to be applied to principal only. I was then told the funds would be returned unless I paid off the remaining balance within approximately 24 hours. Because of that pressure, I sent an additional wire for {$4400.00}. Unlike the first wire, this second wire was marked Apply to Payoff. The different instructions on the two wires show the difference in intent : the first payment was principal-only, and the second payment was only sent after I was told the first payment would be returned unless I completed the payoff. The total wired was {$140000.00}. My concern is that a borrower who makes a large principal-only payment should not be forced into an all-or-nothing payoff decision under threat of having the payment returned. This type of communication could pressure borrowers into sending funds they did not intend to send, or prevent borrowers from making legitimate principal-only payments. I am not primarily seeking personal financial relief. I am filing this complaint because I believe this payment-handling practice should be reviewed so it does not happen to other borrowers. I would like Planet Home Lending to review the handling of this transaction and provide a written explanation addressing the following : 1. Why a wire clearly marked Apply to Principal was treated as a payoff ; 2. Whether Planet Home Lending allows borrowers to make large principal-only payments without paying off the full loan ; 3. The policy, servicing rule, investor requirement, or other basis Planet relied on when it threatened to return the funds unless I paid off the remaining balance ; 4. Whether my loan was current at the time the {$140000.00} principal payment was received ; 5. How Planet trains representatives to handle large principal-only payments ; 6. Whether Planet will review the call handling and communication used in this matter ; 7. What steps Planet will take to ensure borrowers who clearly designate payments as principal-only are not misclassified as payoff borrowers or pressured into sending additional funds unnecessarily. My goal is for Planet Home Lending to review this process and ensure that future borrowers are clearly informed of their options when making a principal-only payment, especially when the payment is large. A principal-only payment should not be automatically treated as a payoff when the borrowers written instructions say otherwise. Attachment 1 shows the first wire request for {$140000.00}, which was marked Apply to Principal. Attachment 2 shows the second wire request for {$4400.00}, which was marked Apply to Payoff. These documents show that the first wire was intended as a principal-only payment, while the second wire was sent only after I was told the first payment would be returned unless I completed the payoff.

complaints.issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
complaints.narrative: Im filing a complaint against " CAINE WEINER '' because they are reporting a collection account ( original creditor listed as XXXX ( Insurance ), account # XXXX ) that is completely unverified. I never gave permission for them to report anything to the credit bureaus. After I was notified of this collection, I immediately requested proper validation. But they didnt provide anything, no signed agreement, no breakdown of the amount theyre claiming I owe, and no proof they have the legal right to collect this debt. Thats a direct violation of 12 CFR1006.34 ( b ) ( 5 ) of Regulation F, which says collectors must provide full debt verification when the consumer requests it. They also failed to give me a fair opportunity to dispute it, violating 12 CFR1006.34 ( c ) ( 4 ) ( i ). Even though they didnt validate the debt, they still went ahead and reported it to the credit reporting agencies. That is both deceptive and illegal under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, specifically 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 7 ) ( A ), which says they cant furnish information to credit bureaus without giving the proper disclosures and the chance to dispute it. They also violated 15U.S.C. 1681b, which says only accounts with a permissible purpose can be included in a consumer report. This account never had my permission or involvement, so theres no valid reason it should be reported under my name. This has caused serious and unnecessary harm to my credit and reputation. Im asking the CFPB to investigate this company and require them to : Stop all credit reporting related to this unverified account. Delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies ; Provide full documentation proving the debt is real, including a contract with my signature, proof of the original creditor, and proof theyre legally authorized to collect it. If this matter is not resolved, Im prepared to pursue legal action under 15 U.S.C.1681n and 1681o for willful and negligent noncompliance with the FCRA . Their refusal to follow federal law should not be ignored. Please help get this account removed from my report and make sure theyre held accountable for these violations.

This condition was never disclosed in the written clarification provided to me, nor was it communicated as a requirement when I was instructed I could continue trying the product until approximately XX/XX/XXXX. On the contrary, the company continued encouraging me to try additional product shipments after my cancellation request had been ignored and after I had already informed them the product was not working for me and that I intended to rely on the advertised 45-day money-back guarantee. It was only after additional questioning on my part that the company disclosed the additional shipment allegedly would not qualify under the guarantee, at which point I declined the shipment again. They did, however, after much time and effort and multiple emails, eventually refund me for that second shipment, calling it a " courtesy '' instead of taking accountability for shipping it out and causing a bigger issue to begin with. The dispute and complaint therefore are not simply about returned merchandise. The issue is that : The merchant clarified their terms in writing when I asked for clarity due to their ambiguity, I relied on those representations, The merchant later contradicted those representations, And Capital One appears to have evaluated and interpreted the dispute solely under the merchants original ambiguous generalized terms and conditions rather than the documented communications that modified and clarified those terms. Additionally, the merchants current interpretation effectively means consumers do not actually receive the full advertised 45-day trial period, because the merchant later asserted the product must also arrive back at their facility within that same timeframe a material condition that was never clearly disclosed nor represented, and completely contradicts their advertised 45 day money back risk free trial. I respectfully request : Reconsideration and reclassification of this dispute under misrepresentation and failure to disclose material conditions, Review of the merchants written communications in conjunction with the dispute, Clarification regarding why documented merchant representations were disregarded in favor of ambiguous and generalized terms that the merchant itself later modified and clarified through direct correspondence. I would also like this complaint to include concerns regarding the handling of this matter by Capital One representative XXXX. This complaint is filed jointly by the primary borrower and the co-signer of an Ally Financial auto loan dated XX/XX/XXXX. The loan was for approximately {$34000.00} financed at 13.94 percent APR for 84 months at {$650.00} per month, secured by a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. Shortly after origination, two add-on products ( a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX for {$2800.00} and an XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX for {$1200.00} ) were canceled. The originating dealership processed the cancellations and issued a check dated XX/XX/XXXX in the amount of {$4100.00} payable to Ally Financial. The check stub clearly designated the funds as cancellation refund proceeds intended to reduce the loan principal. Ally Financial received the check but mishandled it. According to Allys own official Payment History letter dated XX/XX/XXXX, Ally applied {$4000.00} to principal and diverted {$92.00} to finance charges, contrary to the checks designation. The same transaction was logged in Allys customer app with the description unknown, despite the check stub clearly identifying its purpose. Allys system then performed repeated internal Reallocations that spread the cancellation refund across future scheduled payments instead of treating it as a one-time principal reduction. The result was that Ally generated and delivered seven consecutive monthly billing statements ( XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX ) showing Amount Due : {$0.00} and Statement Total : {$0.00}. Voluntary payments were made during this period because the borrowers knew the loan still existed. Beginning with the XX/XX/XXXX statement, billing returned to non-XXXX amounts and regular monthly payments resumed. However, according to Allys own official Payment History letter, five of the last six consumer payments ( XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX ), totaling {$3000.00}, were applied 100 percent to finance charges with {$0.00} applied to principal. On a properly amortized simple interest installment loan, this is inconsistent with how the loan was supposed to be administered under the terms of the contract. Compounding the misapplication, Ally is reporting different balances to the consumer and to the credit bureaus on the same date. As of late XX/XX/XXXX, the Ally app showed an outstanding balance of {$30000.00} while the credit bureaus were reporting {$31000.00}, a {$1500.00} discrepancy between Allys own records on the same date. After dispute letters were sent in late XX/XX/XXXX, the bureau-reported balance dropped to {$30000.00} ( a {$950.00} reduction far larger than a normal monthly payment would produce on this balance ) while the Ally app figure has not changed. Ally appears to be making piecemeal bureau-side adjustments without correcting the underlying internal account. Based on the math, the correct outstanding balance as of late XX/XX/XXXX should be approximately {$28000.00}. Ally has collected approximately {$1300.00} in finance charges that were not owed under the terms of the contract, and this excess grows each month the misapplication remains uncorrected. The inflated payoff figure is also blocking the sale of the vehicle. There is a documented {$21000.00} buyer offer, but no buyer will close when the lenders quoted payoff does not match what the math supports. Direct resolution was attempted before filing this complaint. Formal letters were sent by certified mail to Ally Financial and to all three credit bureaus. On XX/XX/XXXX, Allys Executive Customer Relations team acknowledged receipt and assigned a file number, stating only that they are researching the concerns without addressing any of the substantive points. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX acknowledged the bureau dispute and opened the statutory investigation under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. During the active dispute period, Ally has continued making bureau-side adjustments without addressing the underlying account. The conduct described is consistent with a documented pattern of consumer complaints against Ally Financial i

Subject : Consumer Complaint Regarding Citibank Credit Card, Account Access Failure, Lack of Billing Transparency, and Credit Reporting Risk Monday, XX/XX/year> To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding Citibanks handling of the transition of my XXXX XXXX credit card account from XXXX to Citibank. Citibanks servicing failures have left me unable to access my account, review my statement, verify transactions, confirm whether my card or statement was properly delivered, or make an informed payment before my upcoming due date. I contacted Citibank on XX/XX/XXXX in attempt to gain access to their online portal for the first time since my account was switched from XXXX to Citibank. Upon connecting with a representative, I was informed that my payment was due in two days. If I had not called, I would not have known about the due date as a statement was not mailed to my home and I did not receive an electronic notification The representative was unable to provide access Citibanks online system and I still have not been provided with a timely alternative means of reviewing my statement or transaction history. I do not know whether the replacement card was lost in the mail, whether my statement was properly delivered, or whether there are any unauthorized or fraudulent charges on the account. When I contacted Citibank, I was told that the bank could accept a payment over the phone, but representatives would not provide the transaction information necessary for me to verify what I would be paying. I was also told that it would take approximately seven days to receive a statement, despite the fact that my payment deadline was imminent. This creates a serious consumer-protection concern. Citibank is effectively placing me in the position of either paying an unverified balance blindly or risking late fees, adverse credit reporting, and harm to my credit score because Citibank has failed to provide timely access to basic account information. I am particularly concerned that Citibank may assess late fees or report negative payment information to credit bureaus despite the fact that any payment delay would be caused by Citibanks own transition, account-access, and servicing failures. A consumer should not face financial penalty or credit harm because a bank can not provide timely access to statements, transaction information, or account-management tools. This issue also raises concerns about fraud prevention and consumer account security. Because I can not access my account or review recent transactions, I can not determine whether unauthorized charges have occurred. Citibank has not provided an adequate process for me to verify the balance before payment, nor has it provided meaningful support to resolve the access issue before the due date. The transition from XXXX to Citibank appears to have been poorly executed from a consumer-servicing standpoint. Customers should not be transferred into a system where they can not access their accounts, can not review statements, can not verify transactions, and may still be subject to late fees or credit consequences. This reflects a failure to manage a major account transition in a manner that protects consumers.
