I am filing a complaint regarding inconsistent and inadequate explanations related to over-limit transaction approvals on my Apple Card issued by Goldman Sachs. On XX/XX/year>, my Apple Card account balance exceeded my credit limit. My credit limit is {$5300.00}, and my account balance was {$5400.00}. On that same date, I was charged {$100.00} in interest. Despite the account already being over the limit, on XX/XX/year>, a merchant transaction in the amount of {$61.00} was approved on the account. On XX/XX/year>, I contacted Apple Card customer service to ask why the transaction was approved despite insufficient available credit. The initial representative stated that the transaction was approved because it was pending and that the money was coming back. This explanation did not accurately explain how authorization decisions work for available credit, as pending transactions still impact available credit and authorization decisions. I was also told that it doesnt matter what my credit limit is, if a transaction is attempted it will be approved. I requested escalation to a supervisor. During that conversation, I was told that the transaction is still pending, so it may not be affecting my credit limit, even though it had already been approved. I then specifically requested a copy of the policy, terms, or disclosure stating that transactions may still be approved after an account exceeds its stated credit limit. No policy, written explanation, or supporting documentation was provided despite my request. I escalated the problem and had a case opened. On XX/XX/XXXX, after the case was reviewed, I received a call from a supervisor and representative. I was again told that the result of the escalation states verbatim, We can not block or decline merchants from charging your account. They advise you to contact merchants and update the payment info if you no longer wish for them to charge the card. This response still does not explain why a transaction was approved after the account had already exceeded its stated credit limit, nor does it explain the issuers authorization practices regarding over-limit transactions. My concern is not simply that the transaction was approved, but that representatives provided contradictory and inadequate explanations and failed to provide any written policy or disclosure supporting the practices being described. I am requesting a clear written explanation of : 1. Under what circumstances Apple Card/Goldman Sachs authorizes transactions above the credit limit, 2. Whether recurring or merchant-specific transactions are treated differently, 3. Why this specific transaction was approved despite insufficient available credit, 4. Why customer service representatives provided contradictory explanations, 5. Why I was not provided the policy or disclosure I requested regarding over-limit transaction approvals.

complaints.issue: Problems at the end of the loan or lease
complaints.narrative: I am disputing the accuracy of a deficiency balance Hyundai Capital America is reporting on my credit file in the amount of approximately {$26000.00}, arising from a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX ) financed through Hyundai Capital America. The vehicle was financed in XX/XX/XXXX. I stopped making payments in early XXXX. In approximately XX/XX/XXXX, the vehicle was left at a Hyundai dealership in XXXX, Maryland. I did not sign any voluntary surrender or repossession authorization, and I retained no surrender documentation because none was executed. The vehicle was left via a night drop marked for service, not surrendered to the lienholder. Hyundai Capital America subsequently took possession of the vehicle and disposed of it at auction, applying the proceeds against the loan and reporting a deficiency balance of approximately {$26000.00}. My dispute concerns the following : No voluntary surrender authorization exists. I never signed any document authorizing Hyundai Capital America to take possession of or dispose of the vehicle. I did not receive a Notice of Disposition ( Notice of Sale of Vehicle ) as required under Maryland Commercial Law 9-611 and the Maryland Credit Grantor Closed End Credit provisions ( Md. Code Comm. Law 12-1001 et seq. ) prior to the disposition of the collateral. The address Hyundai Capital America had on file ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, MD XXXX ) was vacated by me in XX/XX/XXXX, more than a year before the vehicle was disposed of. I received no notice of disposition at any address. Hyundai Capital America had alternative means of contacting me the dealership was in active telephone contact with me yet I was never provided proper notice of the sale, my right to redeem the collateral, or an accounting. Under Maryland law, a secured party 's failure to provide proper notice of disposition affects its right to collect a deficiency. A deficiency that is not legally substantiated can not be accurately reported as an owed debt. I am requesting that Hyundai Capital America provide : A copy of any signed voluntary surrender or repossession authorization bearing my signature. A copy of the Notice of Disposition / Notice of Sale of Vehicle sent prior to the auction, including the specific address it was sent to and proof of mailing. An itemized accounting of the auction sale, including the sale price, all fees and charges applied, and the calculation of the deficiency balance. Documentation that the disposition was conducted in a commercially reasonable manner as required under Maryland Commercial Law 9-610. If Hyundai Capital America can not substantiate compliance with Maryland notice and disposition requirements, the reported deficiency balance is not legally substantiated and its reporting on my credit file is inaccurate. I request that the tradeline be deleted from all credit bureau reports.

Despite this history, American Express subjected me to four separate financial reviews. Three of those reviews were immediately closed without requiring any documentation whatsoever, which strongly suggests the underlying triggers were unsupported or erroneous. During the most recent review, however, I was asked to provide banking documentation and statements, which I promptly supplied in full compliance with their requests. These limitations were not only disproportionate to my financial profile and account history, but also inconsistent with the risk profile I had demonstrated for over a decade. Most notably, my charge card which historically operated under American Expresss No Preset Spending Limit framework was effectively constrained to a severely reduced spending capacity. This occurred despite no history whatsoever of abuse, delinquency, elevated risk behavior, or inability to pay. What makes this situation especially troubling is the inconsistency in American Expresss own underwriting and risk assessment systems. After these adverse actions occurred, I logged into my American Express account and utilized the platforms internal Increase spending limit / spending limit review functionality. During that process, American Express requested that I link external bank accounts for evaluation purposes. I linked the exact same bank accounts and financial information previously submitted to the Financial Review department the same information that had allegedly been deemed insufficient. Remarkably, American Expresss automated internal system subsequently approved an increase in my available spending capacity from approximately {$6000.00} to {$10000.00} based on that same data. This directly contradicts the conclusions previously reached by the Financial Review department and strongly suggests serious inconsistencies, flaws, or errors in American Expresss underwriting and review processes. From a risk management and banking standpoint, this raises significant concerns regarding : - inconsistent application of underwriting standards ; - potentially defective algorithmic risk modeling ; - lack of transparency in adverse action determinations ; - and improper treatment of longstanding low-risk customers. Under Louisiana Revised Statute XXXX, a creditor is strictly barred from seeking a deficiency judgment unless the property is sold with a lawful appraisal. 21st Mortgage failed to serve the required 7-day appraisal notice, meaning the remaining debt is legally dead and unenforceable under Louisiana civil code. Furthermore, a representative from 21st Mortgage actively engaged in consumer deception on the phone. She explicitly told me that they " know Louisiana law '' but claimed the strict appraisal rules " do not apply because the home is a moveable or mobile home. '' This is a blatant, bad-faith misrepresentation of Louisiana law XXXX La. R.S. 13:4106 explicitly states that a deficiency is prohibited without appraisal whether the property is " movable, immovable, or both. '' Additionally, La. R.S. 9:5363.1 strictly mandates qualified appraisals for factory-built and mobile homes to protect debtors from this exact type of predatory behavior. The representative also admitted the home has already been sold, yet claimed it " takes three months '' to determine what I owe them, keeping this illegal threat hanging over my head as an intimidation tactic to force a voluntary payment on an uncollectible debt. I demand that 21st Mortgage permanently cease and desist all collection activity, mark this account as closed with a {$0.00} balance, and immediately stop harassing me.

Because I was enrolled in paperless billing, I had no expectation of receiving paper statements. Synchrony 's obligation to notify customers of impending promotional expiration does not disappear in a paperless environment ; it shifts to the email channel. I did not receive adequate email notification warning me that my promotional balance needed to be paid in full before expiration to avoid deferred interest charges. The deferred interest product itself is structured in a way that the CFPB has previously found to be harmful to consumers : interest accrues silently for the entire promotional period and is assessed in full if even a small balance remains at expiration. Minimum payment amounts set by Synchrony ( {$110.00} to $ XXXX ) were insufficient to pay off the promotional balance by the expiration date, yet Synchrony did not prominently communicate this gap to me. I am requesting that Synchrony Bank waive or refund the {$2100.00} deferred interest charge applied on XX/XX/XXXX, as well as the {$120.00}, {$120.00}, and {$30.00} in charges that followed directly from that event, for a total of {$2300.00}.

complaints.issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage
complaints.narrative: I am filing this complaint about Chases handling of a pending mortgage assumption arising from a divorce-related property transfer. The purpose of the assumption is to place the existing mortgage into my name alone and remove the other party from liability, consistent with the divorce and property settlement documents already provided to Chase. The process has been pending for an extended period and has been materially delayed by repeated cycles of document requests. Chase issued formal Requests for Missing Information dated XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. Chase also sent additional follow-up requests by email, including requests for refreshed asset statements and pay documentation, before the file could proceed further. I responded to these requests through multiple submission packets, including those submitted on or about XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, along with interim supplements when updated statements or retransmissions were needed. A recurring issue is that Chase has repeatedly requested refreshed versions of the same core document categories, especially current pay documentation and statements from the same savings account. In my XX/XX/XXXX response to Chases XX/XX/XXXX request, I specifically advised that the XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX savings account statements were the same statements previously sent in response to a prior request. Chase later requested the same category of statements and additional paystub coverage again. The file has been represented as having gone to underwriting multiple times, and each time I have been given a general 30 to 50 day timeframe for a decision. After that timeframe passes, the file is returned to assumptions with requests for newly current documents, without a clear explanation of why a decision was not made while the previously submitted documents were current and in Chases possession. In addition, Chase has later identified technical requirements in documents that had already been submitted months earlier, rather than identifying those issues when the documents were first reviewed. For example, letters of explanation that were previously submitted were later identified as needing to be dated and signed by hand, even though those concerns were not clearly raised when the documents were originally provided. I contacted Chase again and obtained an escalation reference number. I was told that an assumptions manager would provide direct information about who is assigned to the underwriting case, and that an escalations manager assigned to my case would call within 24 to 48 business hours. I also obtained a direct number for the escalation team. During the resulting escalation call, Chase stated that it could not guarantee that updated documents would not be requested again after 30 days had elapsed, that I could not speak with anyone assigned to my case in underwriting, and that no timeline could be provided beyond the general 30 to 50 day estimate. I am filing this complaint because the assumption process has become a cycle of repeated document refreshes, unclear status updates, return from underwriting without a decision, and failure to issue a timely decision. I want Chase to assign a responsible escalation manager with authority to track the file, confirm the current underwriting status in writing, identify the assigned underwriting contact or unit, stop issuing rolling duplicate document requests without explanation, and promptly issue either an assumption decision or a specific written explanation of any truly remaining deficiency. If Chase claims that updated documents are required because prior submissions became stale, I want Chase to explain why the file was not reviewed or decided while those documents were current and in Chases possession, and what specific steps Chase will take to prevent the same issue from recurring after any updated submission.

RE : Complaint AgainsXXXX XXXX XXXX Mortgage Servicing Misconduct, Inadequate Disclosure, and Loss Mitigation Concerns To Whom It May Concern : I am submitting this complaint regarding the servicing and loss mitigation handling of my FHA-backed mortgage loan by XXXX XXXX during and immediately following a XXXX XXXX XXXX. From XX/XX/XXXX through XXXX XXXX I suffered a severe multi-system medical XXXX involving XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX transport, prolonged XXXX, XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. During this period, I lacked the functional ability to reasonably manage complex financial and legal affairs. Upon partial recovery, I learned my mortgage servicing had transferred from XXXX to XXXX XXXX and that my home was facing foreclosure risk. I repeatedly informed XXXX representatives that my objective was to save my home and bring my mortgage current. XXXX representatives discussed what was described to me as an FHA Payment Supplement / partial claim option. I was specifically advised that this program would bring the delinquent balance current while reducing monthly principal and interest payments without permanently restructuring my primary mortgage terms. I was further advised that completion of a 90-day trial payment period would demonstrate eligibility. I successfully completed the required trial payments. However, after completion of the trial period, XXXX mailed permanent loan documents containing material terms that had never been disclosed during the trial process or prior communications. These documents : * Modified the primary mortgage loan; * Increased the interest rate ; * Extended the mortgage term approximately 30 years ; and * Included a separate FHA-related agreement. I immediately contacted XXXX and advised that these were not the terms that had been represented to me. I repeatedly requested : * A detailed itemization of all fees and charges; * Clarification regarding the modification structure ; * Alternative loss mitigation options; * Time to consult with HUD counselors ; and * Clarification regarding foreclosure activity and deadlines. Despite these requests, XXXX failed to timely provide a complete accounting and repeatedly advised me that I was running out of time to act. Representatives provided inconsistent and contradictory information regarding available options. I believe XXXX XXXX failed to provide adequate disclosures, failed to provide requested accounting information, provided materially inconsistent representations regarding loss mitigation terms, and failed to ensure informed understanding of the agreements presented to me during a period of extreme medical vulnerability. At the time, we reasonably believed the communications and wire instructions were authentic and associated with the legitimate title company handling our transaction. XXXX XXXX XXXX advised us that the claim status was collection pending while recovery efforts were ongoing. We were later informed that the claim had been closed ; however, XXXX XXXX XXXX has since reopened the matter for reconsideration. We also immediately reported the matter to the FBI/XXXX and the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX To date, only approximately {$18000.00} has been recovered, leaving nearly {$190000.00} unrecovered. We recently spoke directly with an FBI representative, who advised that they are attempting to assemble information for potential review by the U.S. Attorneys Office. This situation has been absolutely devastating to our family emotionally and financially. We understand that fraud investigations can take time ; however, the lack of urgency, communication, empathy, and transparency we have experienced from both XXXX XXXX XXXX and American Express National Bank throughout this process has been shocking and deeply discouraging, especially given how quickly we reported the fraud after discovering it. We are extremely concerned about the handling of the receiving account at American Express National Bank after notice of fraud was provided. Given the speed with which notification and recall efforts were initiated, we are requesting a full accounting and timeline from American Express National Bank regarding when the receiving account was frozen or restricted, when recall and recovery requests were received and acted upon, whether funds had already been withdrawn or transferred prior to action being taken, what actions were taken to attempt to preserve or recover the wired funds after notification of fraud, and whether suspicious activity reviews were initiated on the receiving account. As consumers who acted in less than 24 hours of discovering this fraud, we believe we did everything reasonably possible to mitigate the loss and are seeking transparency, accountability, and any remaining opportunity for recovery. A fair resolution would include a complete written timeline and accounting of actions taken by American Express National Bank after notice of fraud, disclosure of whether internal fraud protocols were followed, any additional recovery efforts available, and consideration of reimbursement or other remedies given the rapid reporting of the fraud and substantial unrecovered losses.

I disp uted the charge because I believe the merchant engaged in deceptive and unfair business practices, including misrepresentation of the products, possible counterfeit goods, and charging an amount that was not properly disclosed during the sales process. During the transaction, I believe I was pressured into purchasing products represented as legitimate medicinal goods. I do not believe Citi adequately considered the evidence provided or explained why it was rejected. I believe this handling may not comply with the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) and Regulation Z, which require credit card issuers to conduct a reasonable investigation of billing disputes and explain the results of the investigation. I am seeking regulatory review of Citis dispute handling process, transparency, and compliance with consumer protection requirements relating to disputed credit card transactions involving potentially counterfeit or materially misrepresented goods.

XXXX XXXX | XXXX, DE XXXX Re : Formal Written Appeal of Dispute Determination Case No. : XXXX Account : XXXX XXXX XXXX ending XXXX Amount : {$180.00} Merchant : XXXX XXXX XXXX Dear Barclays Dispute Resolution Department, I am writing to formally appeal the determination issued in the above-referenced dispute, in which Barclays concluded I am responsible for the {$180.00} charge by XXXX XXXX XXXX. SERVICES WERE NEVER RENDERED The reservation was booked with incorrect dates. I promptly contacted XXXX to request a date modification a standard accommodation offered by virtually all legitimate travel merchants. XXXX refused any modification. As a direct result, I did not stay at the property. No hotel room was occupied. No services were rendered. A charge for services never provided is not a valid transaction. Under the FCBA, a cardholder is not obligated to pay for goods or services not received. Super.coms retention of {$180.00} for a stay that never occurred constitutes unjust enrichment and an unfair billing practice. II. REQUEST FOR MERCHANTS EVIDENCE Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1666, I formally request a complete copy of all documentation and evidence submitted by XXXX in response to this dispute. I am entitled to review the basis upon which Barclays reversed its provisional credit before this matter is considered final. III. GROUNDS FOR REVERSAL Barclays decision to side with the merchant without affording me an opportunity to review and rebut their submission is procedurally deficient. Specifically : 1. Non-delivery of services is an absolute defense regardless of a merchants cancellation policy. A policy permitting retention of full payment for a room never occupied is unconscionable and unenforceable. 2. XXXX refusal to accommodate a simple date correction not a cancellation left me with no viable alternative. The error was correctable at no cost to the merchant ; their refusal was unreasonable. 3. No-refund policies can not lawfully override the fundamental principle that payment is owed only for services actually rendered. IV. DEMAND I respectfully demand the following : 1. Immediate reinstatement of the {$180.00} provisional credit as a permanent credit to my account ; 2. Production of all documentation submitted by XXXX in this dispute ; 3. A full re-review of this matter in light of the facts set forth herein. If Barclays declines to reverse this determination, I will file formal complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency ( OCC ), and the New York Attorney Generals Office of Consumer Frauds and Protection, and will pursue all available remedies under applicable law. FDCPA 15 U.S.C. 1692g & 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( c ) Section 1 Purpose of This Notice This document serves as both : A formal request for debt verification under 15 U.S.C. 1692g, and A cease and desist demand under 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( c ). I dispute the alleged debt referenced by your company and request full verification. Section 2 Required Debt Verification ( FDCPA 1692g ) Please provide the following documentation : Original creditor information Full account number associated with the alleged debt Itemized breakdown of all amounts claimed ( principal, interest, fees, penalties ) Copy of the original signed contract or agreement Proof of your legal authority to collect ( chain of title, assignment, purchase records ) Date of alleged default Date of last payment Statement confirming whether the debt is within the statute of limitations Your state license number ( s ) and collection jurisdictions Until this information is provided, you must cease all collection activity, including credit reporting. Section 3 Cease and Desist Demand ( FDCPA 1692c ( c ) ) Effective immediately, you must stop all communication with me regarding this alleged debt. Under federal law, you may only contact me to : Confirm that collection efforts are being terminated, or Notify me of specific legal remedies you may lawfully pursue Any other communicationincluding calls, letters, emails, texts, or thirdparty contactwill constitute a violation of federal law. You are also instructed not to contact my employer, family, neighbors, or any third parties. Section XXXX Notice of Intent to Report Violations If you continue collection efforts without providing verification, or if you contact me in violation of this cease and desist notice, I will file complaints with : The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) The Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) My State Attorney General I will also pursue all remedies available under the FDCPA, including statutory damages.

I dispute the validity, accuracy, and ownership of this alleged debt. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( a ), a debt collector is required to provide consumers with a written validation notice containing specific information regarding the alleged debt and the consumers rights. Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1692e, debt collectors are prohibited from using false, deceptive, or misleading representations in connection with the collection of any debt. Further, under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2, furnishers of information to consumer reporting agencies have a legal duty to provide accurate and verifiable information. Reporting disputed or unverified information may constitute noncompliance with the FCRA. At this time, Harris & Harris has failed to provide : Proof I owe the alleged debt A complete accounting of the amount claimed A signed agreement or service contract Documentation showing assignment or transfer of the alleged debt Proof they have legal authority to collect Evidence that proper notice was ever mailed to me Despite the lack of verification, this account has been reported to the credit bureaus and has negatively impacted my credit profile.

complaints.issue: Problem with a company's investigation into an existing problem
complaints.narrative: To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, This letter serves as my formal rebuttal to Global Lending Services ( GLS ) response dated XX/XX/year>. Their reply is incomplete, inaccurate, and fails to address the core issues raised in my complaint. GLS continues to provide generic, dismissive statements that do not reflect the facts, the evidence, or their obligations under the FCRA and other applicable laws. GLS asserts that the loan was processed correctly, yet the underwriting was based on incorrect credit information. I provided GLS with the correct credit scores, which placed the applicants in a lower credit tier and would have resulted in a significantly lower APR. GLS refuses to acknowledge or correct this, despite being notified multiple times. Under the FCRA Furnisher Rule, GLS is required to conduct a reasonable investigation and correct inaccurate information. Instead, they continue to rely on the same canned response that the contract can not be modified, which is not a legal defense to knowingly using inaccurate data during underwriting. GLS also fails to address the fact that a fraud alert existed on my credit file at the time of application. Federal law requires a lender to verify identity before extending credit when a fraud alert is present. GLS did not perform this verification until after the vehicle was delivered and the contract executed. This failure directly contributed to the inaccurate underwriting and inflated APR. GLSs response ignores this entirely. Their attempt to shift responsibility to the credit bureaus is also improper. GLS is the furnisher of the information and is legally required to investigate disputes and correct inaccuracies. Directing me to the bureaus is not a substitute for their statutory obligations. GLS further claims they have thoroughly investigated my disputes. This is demonstrably false. They have ignored the corrected credit documentation, ignored the identityverification failure, ignored the underwriting errors, and ignored the evidence provided. They have issued the same template response repeatedly without addressing the substance of the complaint. No documentation of any investigation has been provided, and no corrective action has been taken. GLS also fails to disclose that XXXX refused to administer arbitration because GLS did not comply with XXXX XXXX XXXX and did not pay the required business fees. Under XXXX Consumer Rule XXXX ( d ), a business that refuses to comply with XXXX requirements waives its right to arbitration, and the consumer is legally permitted to pursue the matter in civil court. GLSs refusal to participate in arbitration is further evidence of badfaith conduct and an attempt to avoid accountability. Their statement that the matter is addressed is simply untrue. Nothing has been corrected. The inaccurate credit information remains uncorrected. The APR remains inflated. The loan has not been rerated. No documentation has been provided. No identityverification explanation has been given. No compliance with arbitration has occurred. No meaningful investigation has taken place. I request that the CFPB require GLS to conduct a legitimate investigation, review the correct credit information, rerate the loan using accurate data, correct the APR, reamortize the loan, correct any inaccurate credit reporting, and provide documentation of their findings. GLS should also be required to explain their failure to comply with XXXX arbitration requirements and their refusal to correct known inaccuracies. GLSs continued refusal to address these issues demonstrates a pattern of noncompliance, badfaith conduct, and disregard for federal consumerprotection laws. Regulatory intervention is necessary. Respectfully submitted,

Midland Credit Managements portal currently reflects the following accounts : XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX Acct : XXXX {$1100.00} XXXX XXXX XXXX : XXXX {$940.00} XXXX XXXX XXXX Acct : XXXX {$560.00} XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX Acct : XXXX {$1100.00} XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Acct : XXXX {$590.00} XXXX XXXX Acct : XXXX {$1100.00} However, only the XXXX and XXXX accounts are currently reporting as Midland Credit Management collection accounts on my credit reports. The remaining accounts continue reporting under the original creditors as charged-off accounts. Additionally, there appear to be duplicated account numbers associated with different creditors/accounts, including : XXXX Acct : XXXX appearing for both XXXX XXXX and XXXXXXXX XXXX Acct : XXXX appearing for both XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX These inconsistencies raise serious concerns regarding : * Accuracy of ownership reporting * Accuracy of balances being reported * Proper assignment and transfer documentation * Potential duplicate or misleading reporting * Reliability of Midlands account records * Verification procedures used before furnishing information to consumer reporting agencies I dispute the accuracy and completeness of all accounts associated with Midland Credit Management and requested formal validation directly through Midlands dispute system. Specifically, I requested : * Proof of Midlands legal ownership or assignment rights * Chain of assignment or sale documentation * Original account agreements/contracts * Itemized accounting records * Verification of balances * Verification of delinquency dates and reporting dates At this time, I am concerned that Midland Credit Management may be reporting or attempting to collect accounts without maintaining accurate and verifiable records. complaints.issue: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement
complaints.narrative: I am filing this complaint against American Express regarding its mishandling of multiple unauthorized transaction disputes on my account ending in XXXX. I timely reported several transactions as unauthorized. American Express initially acknowledged the disputes and issued provisional credits. However, after its alleged investigation, American Express reversed those credits and re-billed the disputed amounts to my account, claiming that the transactions were authorized. American Express has not provided me with any meaningful evidence supporting that conclusion. This is unacceptable. American Express can not simply make a conclusory statement that I authorized the transactions while refusing to provide the documents, records, merchant responses, authorization data, fraud analysis, or transaction-level evidence it allegedly relied upon. The disputed transactions include, but may not be limited to : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX {$420.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX {$600.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX {$47.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX {$23.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX {$75.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX {$57.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX {$120.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX XXXX {$53.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX {$73.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX {$150.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX {$220.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX {$120.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX XXXX {$89.00} XX/XX/year> * XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX {$65.00} XX/XX/year> American Express has placed the financial burden on me while refusing to show the factual basis for its decision. If American Express determined these transactions were authorized, then American Express should be able to identify, transaction by transaction, what evidence supports that determination. I specifically requested that American Express reopen the investigation and provide the documentation used to conclude that I authorized these charges. I asked for the evidence supporting its decision, including merchant documentation, receipts, signatures, card-present or card-not-present data, device information, IP address information, shipping information, authorization logs, fraud notes, investigation notes, and any other records relied upon. Instead of providing the requested documentation, American Express merely told me that the fraud department would contact me. I have spoken with approximately four different representatives, yet I still have not received a substantive response, a written explanation, or the evidence used to deny my claim. That is not a reasonable investigation. That is not transparency. And it does not give me any meaningful opportunity to challenge the result. American Express appears to have reversed provisional credits and re-billed me without providing a proper transaction-level explanation of why my unauthorized-use claim was denied. A generic statement that the charges were authorized is not enough. I am entitled to know exactly what evidence American Express relied upon before forcing me to pay for transactions I disputed as unauthorized. My position is simple : if American Express has reliable evidence that I authorized each transaction, it should produce it. If it can not produce that evidence, then the charges should not remain on my account. I am requesting regulatory assistance because American Express has failed to provide a clear explanation, failed to provide the documentation supporting its decision, failed to meaningfully respond to my request for reinvestigation, and failed to explain how it determined that I personally authorized each disputed transaction.

complaints.issue: Took or threatened to take negative or legal action
complaints.narrative: I am filing this complaint to escalate my ongoing dispute with Carrington Mortgage Services. Carrington claims to have servicing authority on my mortgage, but this assertion is flawed for several reasons. First, I have already sent Carrington a formal Notice of Dispute, along with a recorded county document ( BPA ) that reflects the ongoing litigation. Despite this, Carrington relies on assignments that were created after XXXX XXXX allegedly transferred the loan. These post-litigation assignments can not establish retroactive authority. In other words, Carrington is asserting control based on documents created after the fact, which does not resolve the core standing issues in dispute. I need Carrington to respond comprehensively. I demand that they provide a complete chain of title, starting from the original lender, showing exactly how they claim authority. They need to explain how they can act while litigation and appeal remain pending. Additionally, they must address my prior dispute and the XXXX, and clarify why they are acting on a contested assignment. If Carrington fails to provide a thorough, documented response addressing these specific concerns, I will consider their conduct part of a pattern of evasive or incomplete servicing practices. I expect CFPB oversight to ensure Carrington provides full transparency and properly addresses the pending dispute.

complaints.issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage
complaints.narrative: I am submitting a complaint regarding the handling of my HELOC application process with PNC Bank. Over the course of more than XXXX months, I went through XXXX separate HELOC application processes with PNC, each involving significant time, documentation, underwriting reviews, and follow up communication. The XXXX application stemmed from a rate that was quoted to me online but was later not honored due to what I was told was an internal error on PNCs side. The XXXX application was submitted individually based on assurances that my income profile would qualify independently. After progressing through the process, that application was ultimately denied. The XXXX application, submitted with a co-applicant, progressed significantly further and involved underwriting reviews, appraisal discussions, documentation requests, and repeated follow ups over an extended period of time. During the appraisal process for the XXXX application, I requested additional time for more relevant comparable sales to close before moving forward with the appraisal reconsideration process. While waiting for those comps, my application was closed without notification to me. After I later discovered the closure and spoke with my banker, I was asked to provide the updated comparable sales so management could explore reopening the application. I promptly provided the requested comps and was told the matter would be escalated and reviewed. After sending the requested information, I followed up multiple times via text requesting updates and received no response for an extended period. I was ultimately informed that the application could not be reopened and that the only option would be to start over entirely with a new application despite the significant time already invested in the process. What is most concerning to me is the repeated lack of communication, transparency, and process management throughout these applications. In particular, the XXXX application was closed without notice while appraisal reconsideration discussions were ongoing, and I was later required to restart the process entirely after months of effort. This became especially frustrating after my familys recent car accident, when I communicated that access to funds had become more important and was reassured that the process would be escalated and move quickly if needed. Unfortunately, the communication and follow through afterward did not reflect those assurances. I understand that lenders may ultimately decline or not proceed with applications for business reasons. My complaint is not centered on the underwriting outcome itself, but rather on the handling of the process, the repeated communication failures, and the unnecessary loss of time caused by procedural issues outside of my control.

complaints.narrative: I am filing this complaint regarding multiple denied dispute claims with SoFi ( Claim Numbers : XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, XXXX ) for transactions totaling {$150.00} made with the merchant WHATNOT between XX/XX/year>, and XX/XX/year>. SoFi denied these claims, stating " no error occurred, '' failing to investigate the underlying mechanics of a sophisticated digital bait-and-switch operation. The merchants operation relies on active backend inventory manipulation to defraud consumers. The operation functions as a rigged game : Backend Inventory Manipulation ( The Changing List ) : The platform distributes purchases through a digital randomization list. During the live broadcast, the merchant explicitly displays high-value items to solicit transactions. However, while purchases are actively processing, the merchant secretly alters the backend digital inventory list. By deleting the advertised high-value items from the available pool mid-sale, the merchant mathematically reduces the odds of a buyer receiving those items to zero. Distribution of Undisclosed Items : Because the advertised items are removed from the system, buyers are systematically mailed unadvertised, nominal-value items. These items were never displayed on screen during the broadcast and were never disclosed as potential outcomes prior to purchase, constituting an illegal, undisclosed " floor. '' Fabricated Conclusion ( The Cover-up ) : To evade detection by the platform 's compliance monitors, the merchant waits until the conclusion of the broadcast to open arbitrary packs of irrelevant characters on camera. This acts as a deceptive finale to falsely represent the event as a legitimate, randomized game, despite the advertised items having been removed from the inventory pool long before. Public Documentation of Fraud : I initiated these transactions in good faith, believing I was purchasing the inventory actively advertised. Post-transaction, independent research into public consumer forums revealed that I was the victim of a widely documented, systematic scam. Public consensus confirms these exact mechanicsthe " changing list, '' the " undisclosed floor, '' and the " fake finale '' are known tactics used to defraud buyers on the platform. This operation strictly violates XXXX 's Surprise Sets Policy and Gambling Policy, which explicitly prohibit the alteration of odds mid-sale, the manipulation of inventory, and the use of undisclosed goods. How to review the evidence : SoFi closed the investigation solely because the charges were authorized, neglecting to evaluate the fraudulent mechanicsspecifically the backend inventory manipulationused to secure the authorization under false pretenses. My claim files and the associated merchant screenshots demonstrate that the merchant exclusively advertised high-value items, which directly contradicts the undisclosed, nominal items I received. Desired Resolution : I request that SoFi escalate these claims to a supervisor, review the publicly documented mechanics of the merchant 's inventory manipulation, and issue a permanent credit to my account for the total disputed amount of {$150.00}.

I am submitting this complaint regarding Selene XXXX handling of my mortgage loan and recent loss mitigation review. I recently submitted a request for mortgage assistance and loan modification review and Selene denied the request while providing only a vague and conclusory explanation that I was too many payments behind to qualify. This explanation is both insufficient and inconsistent with prior servicing conduct. Notably, Selene previously approved a loan modification on this same loan despite the account already being beyond the alleged 24-month delinquency threshold they referenced during a recent call with the borrower. During the most recent communication, Selene representatives have repeatedly failed to clearly identify : the actual investor guideline allegedly prohibiting approval the owner or investor of the loan whether the denial was based on investor restrictions or internal servicing policy whether all available modification waterfall options were reviewed the financial analysis supporting the denial Instead of meaningfully discussing available retention options, the conversation was largely focused on encouraging surrender of the property without providing substantive information regarding alternatives, reconsideration, escalation, re-amortization options, extension structures, or any detailed explanation of the review process. This raises serious concerns regarding whether Selene conducted a complete and compliant evaluation of the loss mitigation application. Under Regulation X and RESPA servicing requirements, including 12 CFR 1024.41, mortgage servicers are required to exercise reasonable diligence in obtaining documents and evaluating complete loss mitigation applications. Servicers are also required to provide borrowers with specific reasons for denial sufficient for the borrower to understand the basis of the decision and pursue any available appeal rights where applicable. Selenes generalized statement that the loan is too many payments behind to modify fails to identify : the actual restriction relied upon the applicable investor guideline the Underwriting analysis performed or whether any alternatives to foreclosure avoidance were reviewed This is especially concerning because conventional loan modification programs commonly contemplate capitalization of substantial arrearages, term extensions, and other retention structures for borrowers who are already significantly delinquent. The denial therefore appears either : 1. procedurally defective 2. unsupported by adequately disclosed investor restrictions 3. inconsistently applied or based on undisclosed internal overlays rather than clearly articulated investor requirements Additionally, Selene representatives repeatedly failed to provide meaningful assistance during communications and instead appeared primarily focused on disposition of the property rather than exploration of available foreclosure prevention options

Between XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, the identical merchant posted hundreds of fraudulent charges to the prior card. A {$300.00} XXXX statement credit was applied to my account. On XX/XX/XXXX, I made a second XXXX booking at the same property for XX/XX/XXXX ( confirmation : XXXX ), and a second {$300.00} credit was applied on XX/XX/XXXX. In XXXX XXXX, I cancelled the XXXX XXXX XXXX while retaining a separate, active American Express XXXX Card that carries the identical XXXX benefit. This week, I noticed neither reservation was appearing in My Trips on AmexTravel.com and contacted American Express Travel via chat. Over two sessions spanning multiple hours, I was transferred between at least five agents across the Travel and Card Services teams and received contradictory information. One agent incorrectly told me the reservations would appear in My Trips within 24 hours. A subsequent agent informed me the reservations are permanently tied to the cancelled card, will never appear in My Trips, and can not be modified through any self-service channel. The only option offered was to cancel and rebook under my active card, which would trigger clawback of the {$600.00} in XXXX credits already applied. When I asked agents to identify where this limitation is disclosed in the XXXX XXXX terms, XXXX benefit terms, or AmexTravel.com terms and conditions, no agent was able to do so. A Card Services representative acknowledged in writing during the chat : I acknowledge that there isnt clear disclosure that canceling the Card used to book an XXXX reservation would remove your ability to modify that booking, despite holding another eligible Platinum Card. I searched the XXXX benefit terms and AmexTravel.com terms and conditions myself and found no language disclosing that cancelling a card removes modification access to reservations made on that card, even for active cardholders holding another XXXX XXXX with identical benefits. The only relevant language states that credits may be reversed upon cancellation or modification, language that does not address or disclose the modification restriction itself. As a result, I am currently unable to manage two confirmed, prepaid hotel reservations totaling {$600.00} in applied credits, with no disclosed remedy that does not forfeit those credits. This limitation was never communicated at the point of card cancellation, is absent from all published terms, and applies even to cardholders who remain fully eligible for the XXXX benefit through another active card. Beyond these two specific reservations, this undisclosed limitation materially affects how I am able to use the XXXX benefit going forward. As an active XXXX cardholder, I can not confidently make XXXX bookings on any card I may someday cancel even if I will continue holding another active XXXX Card with the same benefit. Since American Express encourages cardholders to hold multiple cards and regularly evaluates which to keep or cancel, this limitation creates an undisclosed and permanent risk that attaches to every XXXX booking I make. The benefit is marketed as a premium travel perk justifying a {$690.00} annual fee, but the terms as applied contain a material restrictionloss of modification access upon card cancellationthat is nowhere disclosed and that fundamentally undermines the utility of the benefit for any cardholder who manages their card portfolio in the normal course.

I am submitting this complaint regarding severe mortgage servicing misconduct, excessive lender-placed insurance ( XXXX ) practices, escrow mismanagement, restoration underfunding, and improper handling of a VA-guaranteed residential mortgage loan associated with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Dovenmuehle Mortgage , InXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXXlated insurance participants. The subject property is lawfully classified and recognized as a residential single-family dwelling. Prior to a catastrophic fire occurring on XXXX XXXX, 2024, the property was consistently insured and underwritten as residential owner-occupied collateral under comprehensive homeowner insurance policies. Following the fire loss, servicing and insurance participants improperly relied upon post-loss Commercial Risk classifications to interfere with my ability to obtain voluntary residential homeowner insurance coverage while simultaneously imposing extraordinarily excessive lender-placed insurance charges and escrow burdens. The servicers imposed force-placed insurance disbursements and projections exceeding approximately {$20000.00}, {$33000.00}, and {$46000.00} during successive servicing periods despite the property remaining legally classified as residential collateral. These charges created catastrophic escrow shortages and substantially increased my financial hardship. The lenders and servicing participants further refused to fully fund approved restoration obligations despite independent adjusters approving the reasonable and necessary cost of restoration, including electrical reconstruction, structural repairs, and hazardous-condition remediation. As a result, the property remains partially unrestored and in continuing hazardous condition involving unresolved electrical fire-risk exposure. After refusing to fully fund restoration of the electrical systems and fire-damaged components, MVB Bank procured lender-placed insurance coverage through Certain Underwriters at XXXX, XXXX containing materially diminished protections and express exclusions for Fire Damage, Products/Operations liability, Personal and Advertising Injury, and Medical Expense coverage while continuing to charge substantial premiums approaching approximately {$26000.00} annually. The lender-placed insurance policy appeared materially defective and misleading because it excluded Fire Damage coverage despite being issued on residential property collateral located within the XXXX of Virginia that had already sustained catastrophic fire loss and continued to contain unresolved electrical fire-risk conditions. I believe the policy structure violated Virginia Standard Fire Policy requirements under Va. Code 38.2-2101 and 14VAC5-342-50 while simultaneously imposing excessive premiums for materially diminished coverage protections. I further believe the servicers and lender-controlled insurance participants engaged in improper lender-placed insurance practices, unreasonable escrow administration, improper force-placement conduct, failure to reasonably evaluate hardship and loss mitigation options, and potentially unlawful fee structures and servicing practices in violation of RESPA, Regulation X, and applicable mortgage servicing standards governing federally related mortgage loans. I previously requested escrow information, lender-placed insurance information, servicing explanations, hardship assistance, modification review, and restoration-related information, but the servicing issues remain unresolved.

Throughout the following months, I made repeated efforts to communicate with the lender regarding my hardship and my desire to keep the account in good standing. Despite being unemployed, I continued making payments whenever possible. I made payments for XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX, even while facing a complete loss of income. I was not ignoring my obligations. I was doing everything within my power to maintain the account while searching for employment, paying rent, utilities, food expenses, and other essential household obligations. During this period, I contacted the lender numerous timeswell over sixty calls by my records. In nearly every conversation, I explained my circumstances, including my job loss, my active search for employment, and my efforts to remain current on the account. I repeatedly asked whether any hardship assistance, deferment, payment arrangement, or temporary accommodation was available. I was informed that I did not qualify for hardship assistance because the loan was too new. Rather than exploring solutions, the conversations consistently focused on when I could make a payment. At no point did I feel that meaningful consideration was given to the extraordinary circumstances I was facing. While I understand that lenders have policies and procedures, I also believe there should be room for reasonable accommodation when a borrower demonstrates good-faith efforts to communicate and pay despite severe hardship.
